tracks.title: Flask on the Step
tracks.subject: a breakfast-radio host who gets up at half past three, and the sleeping wife who leaves a warm flask of tea on the front step for him every morning

tracks.title: The Tent Has Been to Wales
tracks.genre: 70s UK soft-rock with sax hook (10cc and Gerry Rafferty lineage)
tracks.subject: a man who lent his two-man tent to a friend, who lent it to a cousin, and it has now slept nine strangers across three countries while he has never used it

tracks.title: Monday After Closing
tracks.subject: a woman who winds the eleven antique clocks in a small city museum every Monday after closing, and the one clock she leaves stopped at ten past four on purpose

tracks.title: Side B, Eleven Years
tracks.genre: upright-piano saloon torch ballad (1950s late-night lounge)
tracks.subject: a woman who still has the jazz record a man lent her eleven years ago and has never returned it, because as long as she has it he has a reason to call

tracks.title: Back Pew at Half Past Five
tracks.subject: a Finnish church verger who unlocks the church at half past five every winter morning, and the one stranger who always sits in the back pew for ten minutes and never speaks

tracks.title: Saturday Jar
tracks.genre: Hawaiian slack-key and steel-guitar ballad (island pop, 1970s Gabby Pahinui lineage)
tracks.subject: a honey seller at a Saturday farmers' table who writes a new line on the label of one jar for the same woman every week, and she buys only one jar, so he has shelves of unsent lines at home

tracks.title: Six Weeks Behind
tracks.genre: psychedelic folk (Incredible String Band lineage, acoustic, droney)
tracks.subject: two pen pals since age eleven, one on Orkney and one in Tasmania, whose letters take six weeks each way so each answers a question the other asked in another season

tracks.title: Dear Tommy, Love Me
tracks.genre: 1960s French yé-yé pop sung in English (Farfisa organ, jangling guitar, tambourine, girlish lead)
tracks.subject: a girl who ghostwrites her best friend's love notes to a boy, and the boy's replies keep describing details only she wrote, so she's the one falling for him

tracks.title: Mouthing It at the Back
tracks.genre: Scottish ceilidh folk-rock (accordion and fiddle with a full rock backline, Waterboys and Runrig lineage)
tracks.subject: a minister's speechwriter stands at the back of the hall mouthing every line, then the minister drops her best pun, and she mouths the rest into the silence

tracks.title: Bees in the Sousaphone
tracks.genre: traditional New Orleans Dixieland jazz (collective improvisation, cornet, clarinet, trombone, banjo, tuba)
tracks.subject: a swarm of bees settles in the bell of the sousaphone the morning before the parade, and the beekeeper must be coaxed away from his honey stand to talk them out while the band keeps time

tracks.title: Counter Number Three
tracks.subject: A middle-aged man named Mr. Odell buys a bottle of vitamin C he does not need every Thursday at the same pharmacy counter just to hear the pharmacist, Bernadette, say hello; after eleven bottles she writes her phone number on the receipt.

tracks.title: Odd Days, Even Days
tracks.subject: Sixty-year-old identical twin brothers own one old bicycle between them and ride it on alternate dates, odd days for one and even days for the other, until the 31st of the month starts an argument.

tracks.title: False Bottom
tracks.genre: Canterbury-scene jazz-rock pop (Soft Machine and Caravan lineage)
tracks.subject: A stage magician's assistant who spends every show folded into the false bottom of a trunk, counting the audience's applause from inside, decides tonight that she will take the bow before him, because the trick only works on her cue.

tracks.title: Fresh Paste Friday
tracks.genre: UK freakbeat (1966-67 mod and psychedelic beat)
tracks.subject: A bill-poster pastes gig posters onto the same hoarding by the bus station every Friday morning and finds each one peeled off by Monday, so he starts printing an extra copy for the girl who clearly wants it on her bedroom wall.

tracks.title: Quarter Past Twelve in Almeria
tracks.subject: A stunt gunfighter at a tourist western town in the Almería desert has been shot dead at the same balcony every day at 12:15 for twenty-two years; today a small child in the crowd claps for him alone.

tracks.title: Carrot Nose
tracks.subject: A girl builds a snowman in the park at lunchtime and ties her crush's lost red scarf on it, hoping he walks past and recognises it

tracks.title: Ticket Number Forty-One
tracks.subject: A man pawns his guitar to buy his wife a ring, and the pawnbroker lets him play it every Sunday before the shop opens

tracks.title: Shoe the Horse
tracks.subject: A Midrand farrier can only fit a cart-horse's new shoes while a slow house track plays, because the old horse stamps in time and stands still

tracks.title: Gold Leaf Mistake
tracks.subject: A shop-front sign-writer gilds the name of a new bakery in gold leaf, spells it wrong, and the owner keeps it because queues form to point at it

tracks.title: The Friday Key
tracks.subject: A woman who has wound the town-hall clock every Friday for thirty years is handed a quartz replacement and asks to wind it one last time with the new mayor

tracks.title: Table Four, Table Six
tracks.subject: On a blind date set up by his sister, Colin sits at table four and Jan at table six of a Liverpool tea room, each secretly brought a best friend to spy from the next table, and it is the two spies who start talking.

tracks.title: The Penny Blue
tracks.subject: A woman goes to the Saturday stamp fair in a church hall to buy one gift, keeps returning to the same dealer's table asking for the penny blue, and is really watching his careful tweezers.

tracks.title: Floor Thirty-One
tracks.subject: A Lagos high-rise window cleaner on a rope seat watches a man on floor thirty-one rehearse his resignation speech to the glass every Tuesday, nods him on, and the man finally quits and waves the cleaner in for coffee.

tracks.title: Six Ten at the Swing Bridge
tracks.subject: A swing-bridge keeper on a small river turns the span open at 6:10 every morning for one coal barge, knows its pilot only by her two horn blasts and a lamp, and today leaves the bridge open and walks down to the quay with two cups of tea.

tracks.title: Greensleeves on Every Street
tracks.subject: An ice-cream van driver whose chime box is jammed on four bars of one tune sells out on every estate because children chase it, and decides to build his whole route around it.

tracks.title: I Only Know Your Eyes
tracks.subject: Two day-shift packers on a biscuit factory's custard-cream line fall in love knowing only each other's eyes between hairnet and blue beard snood, and outside the gate she walks straight past him until he cups his hands over his beard.

tracks.title: Eleven Elections
tracks.subject: Two poll clerks share a trestle table in a village hall only on election days, eleven in twenty years, until she catches herself hoping for a snap election and, as the box is sealed at ten, he asks why wait for the next.

tracks.title: Run, Hank, Run
tracks.subject: A wife on the Ocmulgee riverbank in Macon watches a gust lift her husband's auburn toupee off his head and a neighbour's coonhound trot off with it, and has to decide whether to admit she has known since the wedding day.

tracks.title: I Only Asked About the Fountain
tracks.subject: A man new to town goes to his first residents' association AGM only to ask why the square's fountain has been dry since 2016, raises his hand at the wrong moment, and walks home elected treasurer, carrying a biscuit tin with £41.17 in it.

tracks.title: Nana's Got an Anchor
tracks.subject: A grandmother who has never been to sea gets an anchor tattooed on her forearm for her seventieth birthday and hides it under cardigans all summer from her disapproving daughter, who finally rolls up her own sleeve to show a swallow hidden since 1996.

tracks.title: Panel B, Panel B, Panel B
tracks.subject: a man in a Swindon back garden assembling a flat-pack shed on a Saturday and finding the kit has three wall panels stamped B and none stamped C, so he builds it anyway with the window facing the fence

tracks.title: Lemon and Basil
tracks.subject: a woman whose homemade lemon-and-basil candle side hustle takes over her one-bed flat, wax on the hob and boxes on the bed, until the postman says the whole street smells of her and she has sold just four

tracks.title: The Knee That Clicks
tracks.subject: a wife who says she can find her husband in a dark house by the click of his left knee on every step, and he takes her out dancing on their anniversary so she can hear it keep time

tracks.title: Same Heel Again
tracks.subject: a woman who runs a one-person shoe repair kiosk in Lewisham and realises the man who brings in the same brown brogue with a worn heel every second week has been walking it down on purpose

tracks.title: Day Three of the Hiccups
tracks.subject: a man in Croydon who has had the hiccups for three days, working through every cure his coworkers swear by, sugar, a paper bag, drinking upside down, a sudden shout from behind, and none of them working

tracks.title: One Hosepipe Between Us
tracks.subject: a man on an allotment who shares one hosepipe through the fence with the woman on the next plot, and starts leaving tomatoes on her shed step every Sunday until she leaves a note asking him to dinner

tracks.title: Four Kettles Make a Bath
tracks.subject: four flatmates whose boiler dies the week before the landlord's man can come, running every kettle and pan in the house in relay to fill one bath and drawing lots for who gets in first

tracks.title: Tagged at Four Pounds Fifty
tracks.subject: a Saturday volunteer at a charity shop who prices a gold sequin jacket from the donation bags at four pounds fifty, then buys it herself and wears it on the till before the shop opens

tracks.title: Your Sofa, Week Three
tracks.subject: a man sleeping on his friend's sofa for a third week after a flat fell through, folding the duvet into a perfect square by seven every morning and learning to dodge the friend's cat at the fridge

tracks.title: Five Minutes Flat
tracks.subject: a woman training on her living-room rug to hold a plank for five full minutes before her fiftieth birthday, counting on the oven clock while her husband reads the seconds out loud

tracks.title: Clearance Rack Two-Step
tracks.subject: a man who buys cowboy boots off the clearance rack for a Saturday dance and can't peel the bright orange $39.99 sticker off the sole, so every spin on the floor shows the whole room what he paid

tracks.title: Bless You, Forty-One
tracks.subject: a woman in hay-fever season who secretly keeps count of how many times her boyfriend says bless you, and realises on the forty-first sneeze of April that he has never once missed one

tracks.title: Cone Of Shame
tracks.subject: a man whose beagle comes home from the vet wearing a plastic cone after a minor operation and spends the week bumping into doorframes, the coffee table and the cat

tracks.title: Say It Again, Walter
tracks.subject: a woman in her sixties fitted with her first hearing aids, who sits in the car outside the audiologist's office and hears her husband Walter humming along to the radio, something he has apparently done for years

tracks.title: Half-Mast
tracks.subject: a fourteen-year-old who grew three inches over the summer holidays and turns up on the first day of the new school year in last year's trousers, two inches above his socks, and decides to strut it out

tracks.title: Ten More Minutes
tracks.subject: a husband who sets the alarm ten minutes before it needs to go off every weekday so he and his wife can lie awake talking about nothing before the day starts

tracks.title: Wrong Room, Right Boots
tracks.subject: a woman who walks into the wrong room at the leisure centre expecting spin class and finds a Thursday line-dancing class for pensioners, stays out of politeness, and by week three owns the boots

tracks.title: Name on the Hummus
tracks.subject: a woman whose new flatmate writes his name on everything he puts in the shared fridge, so she starts labelling things back, until she sticks a label with her own name on his forehead and he laughs for the first time

tracks.title: Where's Bernard
tracks.subject: a man whose pet tortoise Bernard escapes into the back garden and stays missing for three weeks while the whole family searches, until he finds him asleep inside his own wellington boot by the back door

tracks.title: Glitter Till Wednesday
tracks.subject: a woman who goes to one Saturday warehouse rave in a glitter top and keeps finding the glitter all through the working week, on her keyboard, in her porridge and on her manager's sleeve during Wednesday's budget meeting

tracks.title: Your Side of the Duvet
tracks.subject: a man in Leeds whose wife rolls the whole duvet around herself every night; he buys a second duvet just for himself, and every morning she is under his one anyway

tracks.title: Thursday, Says Dave
tracks.subject: a man in a Salford terrace whose bathroom tap drips all week while the plumber Dave keeps texting 'Thursday', until he starts dancing round the flat to the drip

tracks.title: Day Three Hundred Sixty-Six
tracks.subject: a man whose kettle dies on day 366 of its one-year warranty, who storms the electrical shop with the receipt and a calendar, and is offered ten percent off a new kettle

tracks.title: Somebody Else's List
tracks.subject: a woman who finds a stranger's handwritten shopping list in the pocket of a charity-shop wool coat, buys every item on it and cooks whatever that list was meant to become

tracks.title: Fourteen Across
tracks.subject: four regulars at a Norwich pub stuck all week on 14 across of the Saturday cryptic crossword, until the landlady pulling pints solves it without looking up

tracks.title: No Receipt, No Problem
tracks.mood: cocky, petty and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a Newark guy trying to return a pair of white trainers to a shoe store with no receipt, arguing with the teenage clerk over the scuff on the left toe, and walking out with store credit for exactly one pair of socks

tracks.title: Sunday Collars
tracks.subject: a woman teaching her new boyfriend to iron his own work shirts on a Sunday night: steam hissing, collars first, and the one blue shirt he scorches, which she keeps as a nightshirt

tracks.title: It Comes Back Black
tracks.subject: a London renter at war with a black mould patch on her bathroom ceiling that returns every three weeks no matter how much bleach she uses, until the landlord finally sends someone to fix the extractor fan

tracks.title: Shell on Seven Mile
tracks.subject: a Detroit man whose forty-year-old pet tortoise Big Ron escapes the backyard and is found three blocks away at the car wash on Seven Mile, where the whole crew starts chanting his name

tracks.title: Garage Line
tracks.subject: a retired bus mechanic in Fresno whose HO-scale model railway grows out of the spare room, across the hallway and through a hole in the garage wall, until his wife's car is parked on the street and she asks for a station named after her

tracks.title: One Waffle Each
tracks.subject: a British tourist at a Vienna hotel breakfast buffet who sets her alarm for six fifty-five every morning of the holiday to beat a German family to the only flip-over waffle iron, and on the last day finds the dad has left her the batter jug and a waffle already turning

tracks.title: Coach Twelve, Seat Sixty-One
tracks.subject: two strangers stuck for four hours on a Eurostar halted in a field outside Lille split the one tin of sardines, a squashed baguette and a clementine she had packed, swap numbers on the back of a ticket, and a year later book the same train, coach and seats on purpose, bringing two tins this time

tracks.title: Rocks on the Windowsill
tracks.subject: a woman whose boyfriend spends every weekend splitting shale in a disused Yorkshire quarry and fills her flat with ammonites on the windowsills, a trilobite in the butter dish and a hammer in the dishwasher, and she lists it all while not quite asking him to stop

tracks.title: Shake That Tree, Darlene
tracks.subject: an old Texas couple bringing in their pecan harvest in November with a tree shaker borrowed from the co-op for one afternoon only, the husband clamping the trunk while his wife drives the sweeper, nuts bouncing off the truck roof, both racing the co-op man who is coming at four to take the shaker back

tracks.title: Ride-On Through Bolton
tracks.subject: a council grounds worker in Bolton who mows the roundabouts and grass verges on a ride-on mower every summer, waves at the same bus driver at the same roundabout each morning, and spares one patch of wild orchids on the ring road verge that she tapes off with her own bunting

tracks.title: Send It to the Lab
tracks.mood: swaggering, sheepish and laughing at himself
tracks.subject: a first-year hobby farmer in Ohio who mails a zip bag of his back-field dirt to the state university extension lab, brags to the feed store all month, and gets the report back saying it is mostly gravel and needs two tons of lime

tracks.title: Through the Studio Glass
tracks.subject: a night security guard at a city art museum who falls for the paintings conservator working late on cleaning old varnish off a harbour painting, watching her through the conservation studio glass on every round and bringing her a vending-machine tea at three

tracks.title: One Question at Window Nine
tracks.subject: a man queueing at seven in the morning outside the US embassy in London for his work visa interview, paying a shop round the corner five pounds to hold his phone, rehearsing answers for an hour, and getting asked one question at window nine

tracks.title: Six Hundred Grams
tracks.subject: a hedgehog rescue volunteer in a Sheffield terrace weighing autumn hoglets on kitchen scales at two in the morning, feeding them cat biscuits until each one passes six hundred grams and can be released before hibernation

tracks.title: Grandad Nicked It from Kew
tracks.subject: a Peckham man carrying a six-foot cheese plant in a Lidl bag-for-life to Kew Gardens across London by bus, because his grandad pinched it as a finger-long cutting from the Palm House in 1971 and it has since eaten the whole front room, and the Kew botanist who looks at the leaves, says they lost that exact one in a 1987 storm, and takes it back for the glasshouse with his grandad's name on the label

tracks.title: King Conker
tracks.subject: a primary-school caretaker who spends September soaking and baking conkers from the playground horse chestnut, is handed a conker from the organisers' bucket at the World Conker Championships in Southwick, wins round one and loses round two to a girl from his own school

tracks.title: Touch-Move
tracks.subject: a fifteen-year-old at an under-sixteens rapidplay chess tournament in a Croydon school sports hall who trash-talks only in his head because talking at the board is banned, hangs his queen and still wins on time

tracks.title: Call the Fridgie
tracks.subject: a female refrigeration mechanic in western Sydney fixing the coolrooms of four pubs and clubs on a 46-degree day in Penrith before the Friday rush

tracks.title: Mile Nineteen
tracks.subject: a London Marathon volunteer handing out water at the mile-nineteen station at Canary Wharf, shouting the names written on runners' vests until the last walker comes through

tracks.title: I'll Write It Down
tracks.subject: a husband of twenty-two years who drives his amateur-astronomer wife to Borrego Springs every August for the Perseids and writes down every meteor she calls out, though he never sees one himself

tracks.title: Ring-Pull
tracks.subject: a man combing Tynemouth Longsands with a borrowed metal detector for the wedding ring he lost swimming, while his wife on the steps offers to marry him again with a ring-pull

tracks.title: Under-Nines
tracks.subject: a fourteen-year-old referee at a Sunday-morning under-nines football match on pitch three, shouted at by touchline dads in a league that keeps no score

tracks.title: Somebody Press The Button
tracks.subject: a council events officer whose booked soap-opera vet cancels at four o'clock on the night of the town's Christmas lights switch-on, until a fourteen-year-old Labrador presses the button

tracks.title: Up To My Shoulder
tracks.subject: a Mississippi Delta man noodling for a flathead catfish under a cypress log in the Sunflower River with his bare arm, and the forty-one-pound fish that bites back

tracks.title: Old Sober
tracks.subject: a yakamein seller pushing two coolers on a grocery cart four miles behind a Sunday second-line parade in New Orleans, selling old sober at every stop

tracks.title: Your Ball's on My Side
tracks.subject: a man on a public tennis court whose neighbour on the next court keeps hitting her balls over the net divider every Saturday morning

tracks.title: The Last Piece
tracks.subject: a man who hides the final piece of his partner's thousand-piece jigsaw in his pocket so they can finish it together on a Sunday night

tracks.title: Second Place Marrow
tracks.mood: raw, rueful and funny at her own expense
tracks.subject: a woman losing the village show's biggest-marrow prize to the same retired man for the third summer running, with her allotment marrow on a wheelbarrow

tracks.title: Four A.M. Proof
tracks.subject: the overnight baker at a supermarket in-store bakery waiting on dough to prove at four in the morning while the shelf-stackers argue about football

tracks.title: Minding Your Goldfish
tracks.subject: looking after his crush's goldfish while she is on holiday and reporting its every move by text

tracks.title: Eggshell, Not Satin
tracks.mood: flirty, giddy and a little shameless
tracks.subject: inventing a new paint project every Saturday to flirt with the man at the hardware store mixing counter

tracks.title: Nobody Signed Up
tracks.mood: defiant, campy and laughing at the empty room
tracks.subject: the Wednesday karaoke host at a half-empty bowling alley singing the whole night herself when nobody signs up

tracks.title: One Sink
tracks.subject: two people sharing one small bathroom sink every morning in a new flat

tracks.title: Half-Smoke, All The Way
tracks.subject: a lunchtime food-truck line on a DC sidewalk where the cook calls out orders in rhythm

tracks.title: Tombola In The Rain
tracks.mood: cheeky, soaked and refusing to go home
tracks.subject: a village fete that gets rained off while everyone keeps going under the tea tent

tracks.title: Slide Fourteen
tracks.mood: sheepish, grateful and smiling at himself
tracks.subject: running the lyric slides at a Sunday service and always being one line behind the band

tracks.title: Gate Forty-One
tracks.mood: flirty and unhurried, hoping the delay gets longer
tracks.subject: sharing one phone charger with a stranger at an airport gate during a five-hour delay

tracks.title: Spare Key
tracks.mood: giddy, out of breath, happily in love
tracks.subject: getting a spare key cut for your partner at the key kiosk under the stairs at Waterloo station

tracks.title: Name On The Lid
tracks.subject: four flatmates interrogating each other over a strawberry yoghurt with a name written on the lid

tracks.title: Thirty-First Of January
tracks.mood: frantic and deadpan, a deadline closing in
tracks.subject: filing your tax return online at twenty to midnight on deadline night

tracks.title: Bijou
tracks.subject: a rental viewing in Rathmines with forty other people where the agent calls a cupboard the second bedroom

tracks.title: Padel Court
tracks.mood: furious, proud, ready for the pit
tracks.subject: the council turning the town's only skatepark into padel courts

tracks.title: Wrong Way On Purpose
tracks.mood: cheeky, grown and sweet on her
tracks.subject: a husband who turns left when the whole Friday line dance at the Elks Lodge turns right, so that for one count of eight he is facing his wife of thirty years

tracks.title: Still Blue On Tuesday
tracks.mood: wild, giddy and still covered in paint
tracks.subject: turning up to the office on Tuesday still blue from J'ouvert paint after Labor Day in Brooklyn

tracks.title: Pocket Dial
tracks.mood: tender and blurred, holding on to something ordinary
tracks.subject: a four-minute pocket-dial voicemail of your father washing up and whistling

tracks.title: It's Green, It's Got A Hood
tracks.mood: tipsy and dead serious about a coat
tracks.subject: describing your lost coat to the cloakroom attendant at four in the morning without your ticket

tracks.title: Move The Prius
tracks.mood: petty, loud and very pleased with itself
tracks.subject: a diss track aimed at the neighbour whose Prius blocks your driveway every Thursday

tracks.title: Nine-Volt
tracks.subject: a smoke alarm chirping for a new battery at three in the morning on a ceiling you cannot reach

tracks.title: Fourth Floor Walk-Up
tracks.mood: earnest, out of breath, falling hard
tracks.subject: carrying a friend's sofa up four flights of a walk-up and realising on the third landing that you are in love with her

tracks.title: The Answer Was Canberra
tracks.subject: falling for the captain of the rival team at a Tuesday pub quiz

tracks.title: Gary's Actually Great
tracks.subject: your ex's new boyfriend turning out to be genuinely nice at a friend's barbecue

tracks.title: Miss Gloria's Extension Cord
tracks.subject: a block party whose DJ keeps losing power because the extension cord runs through Miss Gloria's kitchen

tracks.title: Lionel Says Don't Look Down
tracks.subject: being taught the zydeco two-step at a Sunday afternoon dance in Opelousas by a seventy-three-year-old retired mailman

tracks.title: Every Crab Is Kevin
tracks.subject: a wife who names every crab in the tide pools Kevin

tracks.title: Lake Effect
tracks.subject: an overnight snowplough driver in Buffalo during a lake-effect storm who raps about his truck like it is a luxury car

tracks.title: Thirty-Three In The Queue
tracks.mood: too old for it and glad to be there
tracks.subject: queueing for a club where everyone else is twenty

tracks.title: Dad On The Decks
tracks.mood: meeting your father before he was your father
tracks.subject: a sixty-one-year-old father pulling a sheet off two turntables in the loft

tracks.title: Mr Kim Calls Me Professor
tracks.mood: a nickname that turned out to be a prophecy
tracks.subject: a corner store owner who nicknamed a twelve-year-old Professor

tracks.title: Unexpected Item
tracks.mood: being a function until somebody sees a person
tracks.subject: the one human attendant for six self-checkout machines

tracks.title: They Put A Rowing Machine Where My Bed Was
tracks.mood: happy for her and lost at the same time
tracks.subject: coming home to find your childhood bedroom turned into your mother's home gym

tracks.title: Wind Chime
tracks.mood: a grief you have no standing to feel
tracks.subject: the neighbour's wind chime you resented for fourteen years and now miss

tracks.title: Recipe Card
tracks.subject: learning your late mother's handwriting from her recipe cards

tracks.title: Mall Walkers
tracks.subject: walking laps of a shopping mall at seven in the morning with retirees

tracks.title: They Spell It With A C
tracks.subject: ten years of never correcting the spelling of your own name

tracks.title: Jury Summons
tracks.subject: being called for jury duty and wanting to be picked

tracks.title: Sold The Blue Dodge
tracks.subject: selling a dead uncle's pickup and keeping the screwdriver from the door

tracks.title: Thirty Years On Wednesday
tracks.subject: the hairdresser who has kept a standing hour for your mother for thirty years

tracks.title: Vows On A Napkin
tracks.subject: being asked to officiate a friend's wedding and having an empty document called VOWS

tracks.title: Dashcam
tracks.subject: a two-second near-miss on a dashcam you keep reopening at night

tracks.title: Sleep Study
tracks.subject: a night wired up in a sleep clinic, meeting the part of yourself you have never met

tracks.title: Two Exits Past Ardmore
tracks.subject: waiting in a truck outside a diner on I-35

tracks.title: Aunt Rose Won't Sit Down
tracks.subject: an aunt who dances through an entire wedding reception

tracks.title: Dead Mall Security
tracks.subject: a night security guard in a mall with no tenants

tracks.title: Whose Name Is On The Gas
tracks.subject: sorting out a utility bill after someone moves out

tracks.title: Ring Light, Four Dollars
tracks.subject: filming a sponsored post while broke

tracks.title: Hold The Line Open
tracks.subject: a long-distance call

tracks.title: Somebody Left The Porch Light
tracks.subject: coming home after a long absence

tracks.title: Two Lanes Out Of Tulsa
tracks.subject: a two-lane road out of town

tracks.title: Everybody's Fine Down Here
tracks.subject: a pub on the last night before it closes

tracks.title: Held Note
tracks.subject: a long train tunnel

tracks.title: Rearview Saint
tracks.subject: driving too fast at night

tracks.title: Smoke Without A Room
tracks.subject: an apartment emptied of furniture

tracks.title: The Weight Of Small Hours
tracks.subject: sitting up with someone who is ill

tracks.title: Late Set At The Blue Room
tracks.subject: the last set of the night at a jazz club

tracks.title: Generator Song
tracks.subject: a neighbourhood when the power comes back
